findings.text: The narrowed handler now lets a Neo4j failure escape _fetch_code_chunks, and _fetch_code_context's caller loop (the `for group_key, indexed_signals in context_groups.items():` at parallel.py:3724) is not wrapped in try/except — the only handler near it guards the LLM call, not the context build. So a transient planner or connection fault that formerly degraded one group's context to empty now propagates out of enrich_worker to the engine's worker-level handling. That is the intended visibility change (the prior review asked for it), but its blast radius — worker abort versus logged degradation and retry — is asserted by nothing in the diff.

The guard keys on the literal code Neo.ClientError.Schema.IndexNotFound, which appears nowhere else in the repository and is asserted only against a synthetic _neo4j_code in test_absent_index_returns_empty; it is not verified against a live engine's actual code for a missing code_chunk_embedding vector index. The failure direction is safe — a mismatched code raises (visible) rather than returning empty — but whether the absent-index branch is ever taken in production is unconfirmed.

justifications.durability: The new TestCodeContextLookupErrors class pins the narrowed handler: a DatabaseError and an unrelated ClientError must raise, and only the IndexNotFound ClientError may return empty. The guard is demonstrably live, not passing in both states — my mutation back to the broad handler reddens two of the three tests (EXIT=1). Deducted two: the tests exercise the helper directly and never drive enrich_worker, so a regression that re-inlines a swallowing handler at the call site would not be caught; and the propagated failure has no test showing how enrich_worker or the engine surfaces it, so the new failure mode is uncharacterised even though it is the intent of the change.
justifications.evidence: Independent gates reproduced from this review node in my own scratch extraction of eaa54ae5 (/tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/.../ecp-review-eaa54ae5): the head gate ran 54 passed, EXIT=0 with module.__file__ resolving to the scratch tree and cwd the scratch tree (gate-ecp-head-eaa54ae5.log). The reviewed run's own gate logs are readable and complete: base 29bede1cf 49 passed EXIT=0 (gate/base.log), head eaa54ae50 54 passed EXIT=0 (gate/head-narrowed.log). I re-derived the negative control independently: reverting the handler to the former broad `except Exception` in the scratch tree fails TestCodeContextLookupErrors::test_database_error_propagates and ::test_other_client_error_propagates while ::test_absent_index_returns_empty still passes (2 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1; gate-ecp-negctl-eaa54ae5.log), matching the run's own gate/negative-control-handler.log. added_failure_count is 0 because both arms report zero failures. justifications.fit: The delta follows the module's existing shape: the lookup is extracted to the module-level _fetch_code_chunks beside _build_code_context_query, the call site uses await asyncio.to_thread(...) as the neighbouring wiki/context lookups do, the docstring states the mechanism (why only an absent index may yield empty) rather than a plan label, and the two commits are a conventional two-part fix and docs pair. No plan or ticket identifiers appear in source, symbols or comments.
justifications.goal_fidelity: This is the incremental review of the two commits the run gained after its first review (base = the previously reviewed head b3261004e; the run's original base is 516d9dcc2). fbc4dc2b2 narrows the code-context lookup's fault handling and eaa54ae50 records it in the evidence fragment. §18's done-when was already delivered and reviewed at b3261004e (both in-SEARCH predicates pinned, PSRC live counts wiki 4->5 / code 0->3, gate green); the delta adds the fix the first review's follow-on asked for. The inline block in enrich_worker becomes the module-level _fetch_code_chunks (parallel.py:214), which now catches only ClientError carrying Neo.ClientError.Schema.IndexNotFound and re-raises every other Neo4j failure instead of the former broad `except Exception` that logged at debug and returned []. The narrowing is correct against the installed driver (neo4j 5.28.3): Neo4jError.code is a read-only property over _neo4j_code, so getattr(e,"code",None) sees the hydrated code and DatabaseError (a sibling, not a subclass, of ClientError) propagates. Deducted one because the change routes a Neo4j failure out of enrich_worker with no local handler (the group loop at parallel.py:3724 is not wrapped), and no test demonstrates the resulting worker-level behaviour.
justifications.reuse: The extraction removes the previously duplicated inline encoder/graph/format block and gives one place where the code-context lookup is issued and faulted, matching how the file already centralises its query builders. Deducted one only because _fetch_code_chunks remains a private helper reachable in tests yet not exercised through its real caller, so its reuse is local rather than end-to-end.
justifications.scope_discipline: The gained range b3261004e..eaa54ae5 changed exactly the three files this node was dispatched to review (docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/enrichment-context-prefilter.html, imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py, tests/discovery/test_signals_pipeline.py), and the whole run 516d9dcc2..eaa54ae5 changed exactly its five declared write paths.
